90% or so of the AGPase in maize endosperm is extraplastitial, that BT1 is a translocator that facilitates transfer of ADPglucose into amylopasts, and that bt1 mutants have severely reduced starch contents in their endosperms.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the localization and function of AGPase in maize endosperm and the role of BT1 in the transfer of substrates and products of starch synthesis between amyloplasts and the cytosol.
the transport of ADP-gluctose into the amyloptast and its subsequent synthesis into amylopectin.
the localization of starch-synthesizing enzymes and the transport of ADP-gluctose into the stroma of amyloplasts in maize endosperm.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

maize endosperms have an ADP-glucose translocator in their plastid envelope that is required for starch synthesis and that the ADP-gluctose pyrophosphoryylase of maize endosperm is located in the cytosol.
in maize endosomes during the linear phase of amyloplast starch accumulation, the AGPase is located in the cytosol and the BT1 translocates ADP-glucose from the cytosol into the amylopalst.
maize endosperms contain both plastid and extraplastid AGPase, and that the BT1 translocators function in the translocation of ADP-glucoses synthesized in the cytosol into the amyloplant stroma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the BT1 adenylate translocates ADP-glucose from the cytosol to the amyloplastic stroma and that this translocation occurs via a mechanism that is distinct from that for the translocation of ATP and other adenylates.
the maize endosperm amyloplast has a translocator for import of extraplastidiarily synthesized ADP-glucose, but no AGPase.
the BT1 protein facilitates the transport of extraplastidal ADP-glucose synthesized by AGPase and other AGPase-independent pathways into the amylopalst stroma for starch synthesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the amyloplastic AGPase is not a translocator of ADP-glucoses into the amylo-plast stroma.

the amyloplastic ADP-glucose pool in maize endosperm is derived from the cytosol and is maintained by the BT1 translocase, which is the first example of a starch-accumulating tissue in which the ADP-glucosyl acceptor pool is not derived from the plastidial compartment.
maize endosperms have an extraplastidially located, soluble, and active AGPase that is not in the amylo-plasts, but rather in the cytosol and in the plastid stroma.
